summary: The solenoid that switches the unit between load and idle no longer follows the controller. Stuck in the load position the unit compresses past its cut-out point; stuck in the idle position it runs on without ever building pressure. The coil, its wiring and the pilot air are all possible reasons.

checks: Watch the regulator contact while the line pressure passes the cut-out setting; a contact that does not change isolates the fault.
Compare the pressure on the display with a test gauge at the panel to rule out a transducer fault.
Inspect the contact, its pilot connection and its wiring at the pneumatic panel.

conditions.title: Compressor does not unload at cut-out

name: Pressure regulator contact fault
remedy: Clean or replace the regulator contact and renew its pilot connection and wiring as needed. Confirm over several cycles that the contact changes state at the cut-in and cut-out settings and that the unit follows it. Until the repair is made, keep the unit under supervision: with regulation out of action the only protection left against overpressure is the safety valve.

summary: The regulator contact that tells the controller whether the line pressure is satisfied no longer changes state. The controller keeps the unit in whatever mode the stuck contact reports, however the real pressure behaves, so regulation stops working while every sensor still reads correctly.

checks: Watch discharge pressure (P1) at the moment the unit unloads and again when it stops; it should fall away in both cases.
Listen at the blow-down outlet for the vent that should follow every unload.
Inspect the valve, its pilot line and its silencer for blockage or a sticking stem.
Check the condensate drain, because carried-over water is what usually blocks the vent path.

name: Blow-down valve fault
remedy: Free or replace the blow-down valve and clear its pilot line and outlet. Confirm that the vessel vents within the usual time after every unload and after a stop, and that the start current is back in its normal band. Where the motor protection has dropped out repeatedly, have the motor and its protection checked before the unit goes back into normal service.

summary: The blow-down valve does not vent the separator vessel when the unit idles or stops. The element stays under pressure, so the next start is made against a full vessel and the motor draws far more current than it should. A vessel that is never relieved also keeps its heat.

checks: Compare the vessel pressure with the line pressure while the unit delivers; a much larger difference than usual points at this valve.
Rule out a clogged separator element first, since it produces a similar difference but builds up slowly.
Check the valve seat, spring and guide for deposits and for a sticking stem.
Look for oil starvation at the element, which a valve that leaks back will cause.

conditions.note: The vessel pressure stays high while the line stays low; that split points at the valve.

conditions.note: The line pressure stays low while the vessel pressure climbs, which a clogged element does not do.
conditions.title: Discharge pressure high, safety valve blows

name: Minimum-pressure valve fault
remedy: Overhaul or replace the minimum-pressure valve, renew its spring and clear the seat. Refit and confirm over a full cycle that the vessel and line pressures track each other with the normal difference between them and that the loaded current is back in its band. Have the oil circuit checked if the valve was leaking back, because the element may have run with too little oil.

summary: The minimum-pressure valve no longer opens at its setting or no longer holds. Stuck shut, it lets the vessel pressure climb while the line stays low; leaking back, it lets the vessel drain into the line so that the oil circuit never gets the pressure it needs to circulate.

checks: Compare the vessel pressure with the line pressure while the unit delivers and watch how the difference has grown over recent weeks.
Read the running hours since the last separator element change against task 7.3.6.
Check whether the oil grade and the oil change interval have been kept, since the wrong oil blocks an element quickly.
Inspect the downstream filters for oil carry-over.

name: Separator element clogged
remedy: Fit a new separator element and renew its seals and the scavenge line strainer while the vessel is open. Change the oil and the oil filter at the same time if the element blocked early, because that is almost always a sign of the wrong grade or an overdue oil change. Confirm afterwards that the difference between the vessel and line pressures is back to its reference figure.

summary: The separator element is loaded with dirt and oil residue, so the air has to force its way through it. The vessel works at a higher pressure than the line, the motor takes more current for the same delivery, and the element starts to let oil through with the air.

checks: Compare the vessel pressure with the line pressure; heavy carry-over with a normal difference between them points at a damaged element rather than a clogged one.
Check how much oil has been added since the last oil change and compare it with the fill volume.
Inspect the downstream filters and the pipework for oil.
Open the vessel and examine the element and its seal for splits and for tracking marks.

conditions.note: Heavy carry-over with no rise in the vessel pressure at all.
conditions.title: Oil carry-over, high oil consumption

name: Separator element damaged
remedy: Fit a new separator element with new seals and top the oil back up to the mark with the specified grade. Confirm that the carry-over stops and that the oil level then holds between services. Check how the element was damaged before closing the vessel: a collapsed element usually means it was already blocked, and refitting into the same conditions will destroy the new one as well.

signal_moves.note: A torn element does not restrict the flow, so the vessel pressure looks entirely normal.

summary: The element is split, or its seal has failed, so part of the air bypasses the separating media entirely. Oil leaves with the air without the difference across the element growing at all, and the level in the vessel falls much faster than the service schedule expects.

checks: Rule out an overfilled vessel and a damaged element first; both are more common and easier to see.
Check the scavenge line, its strainer and its orifice for sludge and carbon deposits.
Feel the scavenge line while the unit is loaded; a line that is returning oil is warm along its length.
Check the oil change record, since sludge comes from oil left in service too long.
name: Scavenge line blocked
remedy: Clear or replace the scavenge line, its strainer and its orifice, then change the oil and the oil filter so the new line does not block again on the same sludge. Confirm afterwards that the carry-over stops and that the oil level holds. Shorten the oil change interval if the deposits were heavy.

checks: Stop the unit, let the vessel vent and stand, then read the level at the sight glass.
Compare the quantity recorded at the last oil change with the fill volume in section 9.1.
Ask whether anyone has topped the unit up since the last service.

conditions.note: Always the first thing to check after an oil change or a top-up.
conditions.title: Oil carry-over, high oil consumption

name: Oil level above the mark
remedy: Drain the excess oil down to the mark with the unit stopped and the vessel vented, then run the unit and check the level again once it has settled. Confirm that the carry-over stops. Record the quantity that was drained, and note in the service record how much oil the unit actually takes, so the next top-up does not repeat the mistake.

summary: The vessel has been filled above the mark, so oil reaches the separator element faster than it can be separated out. Oil leaves with the air even though every part of the unit is sound. This is the first thing to rule out after any oil change or top-up.

checks: Stop the unit, let the vessel vent and stand, then read the level at the sight glass.
Look under and around the machine for oil at the cooler, the hoses and the shaft seal.
Check the downstream filters for oil, which would point at carry-over rather than a leak.
Compare how much oil has been added recently with the interval in task 7.3.4.
name: Oil level below the minimum
remedy: Top the charge back up to the mark with the specified grade, then find out where it went: an external leak, carry-over through the separator, or a blocked scavenge line. Topping up alone treats the symptom only. Confirm once the level holds that the oil temperature comes back into its normal band.

summary: Too little oil circulates, so the charge that is left has to take up the heat of the whole compression process. The temperature climbs while the unit otherwise behaves normally. A level that keeps falling always has a second cause behind it, which has to be found as well.

checks: Read the service record for the grade and the quantity used at the last oil change.
Look at the oil at the sight glass for a colour or a foaming behaviour that does not match the specified grade.
Check whether the separator element blocked earlier than its interval, which the wrong grade will cause.
Compare the oil temperature and the loaded current with the figures recorded before the last oil change.
name: Wrong oil grade in service
remedy: Drain the charge completely, flush the circuit, and refill with the specified grade and quantity given in section 9.1. Change the oil filter and the separator element at the same time, because the wrong grade damages both. Record the grade used so the mistake is not repeated, and confirm afterwards that the oil temperature and the loaded current return to their normal bands.

summary: The unit has been filled with an oil that is not the specified grade, or with two grades mixed together. It carries heat away less well, drags in the element and separates poorly, so temperature, current and carry-over all move at once without any single part being at fault.

checks: Read the running hours since the last oil filter change against task 7.3.5.
Feel the filter housing while the unit is loaded and compare the temperature across it.
Check the oil change record, since oil left in service too long blocks a filter early.
name: Oil filter clogged
remedy: Fit a new oil filter element and top the charge up to the mark. Change the oil as well if it is anywhere near its interval, because a filter that blocked early is a sign of the oil, not of the filter. Confirm that the oil temperature comes back into its normal band over the next few loaded runs and record the service.

summary: The filter element restricts the oil flow, so less oil reaches the compression element and the injected charge carries away less heat. The restriction builds up slowly across the service interval, and nothing else on the unit changes with it.

checks: Look at the cooler block and the fan guard against the light for a dust or oil film between the fins.
Compare the oil temperature with the ambient temperature over a full cycle; a difference larger than usual points at the cooler.
Confirm that the fan turns freely and at its usual speed, to separate this from a fan failure.
Read the running hours since the last cooler cleaning against task 7.3.7.

conditions.note: The rise is slow and shows in every state, including the idle and stopped phases.
conditions.title: Oil temperature high

name: Oil cooler fouled
remedy: Clean the cooler block, the aftercooler and the fan guard with the unit stopped and isolated, working from the clean side outwards so the dirt is not driven further in. Confirm over the next loaded runs that the oil temperature comes back to its reference figure. Where the site is dusty, shorten the cleaning interval instead of waiting for the warning to return.

checks: Look and listen at the fan while the unit is loaded, and feel for air leaving the cooler outlet.
Isolate the unit and turn the fan by hand to check for a seized bearing or a fouled impeller.
Check the fan supply, its protection and its wiring at the terminal strip.
Look for anything blocking the cooling-air inlet or outlet.

remedy: Free or replace the fan and its motor, clear whatever blocked the airway and restore the supply. Confirm over the next loaded runs that the oil temperature settles at its reference figure. summary: The cooling fan has stopped or turns far too slowly, so almost no air passes through the cooler block. The oil temperature climbs sharply as soon as the unit loads, much faster than a fouled block could explain, and it keeps climbing until the controller stops the unit.

checks: Feel the pipework on both sides of the valve while the unit warms up; a working valve sends the oil to the cooler only once it is warm.
Watch the warm-up curve after a cold start and note whether the oil settles at its working temperature.
Rule out a fouled cooler and a failed fan first, since both are more common.
Inspect the valve element for deposits and for a stem that no longer moves.

remedy: Replace the thermostatic element and clean its housing. Confirm after a cold start that the oil warms up at its usual rate and then settles at its working temperature. checks: Listen at the compression element for a changed running noise, and compare it with how the unit sounded when it was commissioned.

Rule out a clogged separator element and the wrong oil grade first, since both raise the current as well.

name: Airend bearing wear
remedy: Stop the unit and have the compression element inspected and overhauled by a service engineer; a bearing that is allowed to run to failure destroys the rotors as well. Check the drive coupling at the same time under task 7.3.12. Change the oil and both filters after the overhaul, because metal particles will have reached the whole circuit.

checks: Compare the vessel pressure with the line pressure while the unit delivers; a difference that has shrunk over months points at wear.
Rule out a clogged intake filter and a sticking intake valve first, since both also lower the loaded current.
Compare the time a loaded run takes with the reference cycle of section 6.3.
Check the running hours of the unit against the inspection interval.

name: Compression element worn
remedy: Have the compression element inspected and overhauled or exchanged by a service engineer. Wear of this kind is gradual and does not repair itself, so plan the work rather than waiting for a breakdown. Change the oil and both filters after the overhaul and record the new reference figures for the loaded current and the pressure rise per loaded run.

checks: Measure the supply voltage at the terminals while the unit is loaded, not only at rest.
Compare the three phases against each other under load and look for an imbalance.
Feel the motor housing and the terminal box; a supply problem heats the motor while the oil stays normal.
Inspect the supply cable, the fuses and the terminal connections for damage and heat marks.
name: Supply voltage low or unbalanced
remedy: Have the supply, the protection and the connections checked and put right by an electrician; nothing on the compressor side needs work. Confirm after the repair that the loaded current and the start peak are back in their normal bands. A motor that has run for a long time on an unbalanced supply should be checked before the unit returns to full duty.

summary: The supply is weak, or the phases are out of balance, so the motor draws more current for the same work and heats up. A bad start can make the protection drop out before the unit reaches speed. The extra heat is in the motor, not in the oil, which is what gives it away.

checks: Look at the protection relay in the cabinet and confirm that it has tripped.
Read the recorded current of the last loaded runs before the trip and look for a rise.
Check the supply voltage and the balance of the phases before resetting anything.
Turn the compression element by hand, with the unit isolated, to rule out a seizure.
name: Motor protection relay tripped
remedy: Find and remove the reason for the trip first, then reset the relay and start the unit under supervision. A high current from a clogged separator element, a blow-down valve that never vents, a weak supply or worn bearings all trip the same relay, and each has its own repair. Repeated trips with no cause found mean the motor and the relay setting themselves must be checked.

signal_moves.text: Motor current (I1) is persistently near zero while the unit is off.
Load solenoid (D2) is persistently off while the unit is off.

signal_moves.note: No start current appears at all, because the circuit never closes.
signal_moves.text: The current peak at motor start is not reached at start. No start current appears at all, because the circuit never closes.

signal_moves_text: Motor current (I1) is persistently near zero while the unit is off.
Load solenoid (D2) is persistently off while the unit is off.
The current peak at motor start is not reached at start. No start current appears at all, because the circuit never closes.
summary: The motor protection has dropped out and holds the start circuit open. The controller cannot start the unit until the relay is reset, and resetting it without finding the reason for the trip simply repeats the event, usually within a few cycles.

checks: Look at every emergency-stop button on the unit and on any remote station and check that each is released.
Read the message on the display, which names this state directly.
Check the wiring of the emergency-stop circuit if every button is released and the message stays.

conditions.note: Always check this first; it costs nothing and explains most sudden no-start calls.
conditions.title: Compressor does not start

name: Emergency stop active
remedy: Establish why the unit was stopped before releasing anything. Once it is safe, turn the button to release it, reset the message and start the unit under supervision. Where no button is pressed, the fault is in the emergency-stop circuit itself and must be repaired by a qualified person; that circuit is a safety function and must never be bridged.

signal_moves.text: Motor current (I1) is persistently near zero while the unit is off.
Load solenoid (D2) is persistently off while the unit is off.
Intake valve closed (D1) stays on persistently while the unit is off.

signal_moves_text: Motor current (I1) is persistently near zero while the unit is off.
Load solenoid (D2) is persistently off while the unit is off.
Intake valve closed (D1) stays on persistently while the unit is off.
summary: The emergency-stop button is still pressed, or it was never released after an earlier stop. The controller keeps the start inhibited and shows the corresponding message until the button is freed and the message is reset. It is the cheapest possible check and the most commonly missed one.

checks: Compare the display with a test gauge at the pneumatic panel, at rest and under load.
Compare the line reading with the reservoir reading, which shares the same air circuit.
Compare the reading with the state of the low-pressure switch, which is independent of the transducer.
Inspect the transducer, its impulse line and its wiring for moisture, blockage and loose terminals.

conditions.note: The pressure is only low on the display; a test gauge at the panel disagrees with it.
conditions.title: Line pressure below setpoint

conditions.note: The controller never sees the cut-out point, because the reading lags the real pressure.
conditions.title: Compressor does not unload at cut-out

conditions.note: Here the regulation itself also misbehaves, because the controller regulates on the faulty reading.
conditions.title: Reservoir pressure differs from line pressure

name: Line pressure transducer fault
remedy: Clear the impulse line, repair the wiring or replace the transducer, then confirm the reading against a test gauge across the working range. Keep the unit under supervision until the reading is trusted again: with a faulty regulation signal the unit can compress past its cut-out point, and only the safety valve then stands between it and an overpressure.

signal_moves.text: Line pressure (P2) fluctuates intermittently in every state.

signal_moves.note: The reservoir transducer keeps reporting the true pressure, so the two readings drift apart.
signal_moves.text: Reservoir pressure (P5) is unchanged in every state. The reservoir transducer keeps reporting the true pressure, so the two readings drift apart.
Whether a loaded run ends at the cut-out pressure is not reached.

signal_moves.note: The mechanical switch follows the real pressure and contradicts the display.

Low-pressure switch (D5) stays off in every state. The mechanical switch follows the real pressure and contradicts the display.
summary: The line pressure transducer or its wiring reports a value that the pipework does not have. The controller regulates on the wrong figure, so it can hold the unit loaded past the real cut-out point or unload it while the line is still empty, while every other reading stays correct.

checks: Compare the display with a test gauge at the reservoir.
Check the position of the reservoir isolation valves, which produce a real deviation rather than a false one.
Inspect the transducer, its impulse line and its wiring for moisture, blockage and loose terminals.

conditions.note: A test gauge at the reservoir agrees with the line, not with the display.
conditions.title: Reservoir pressure differs from line pressure

manual_ref.title: Reservoir pressure differs from line pressure

name: Reservoir pressure transducer fault
remedy: Clear the impulse line, repair the wiring or replace the transducer, then confirm the reading against a test gauge and against the line reading with the isolation valves open. The unit can stay in service in the meantime, because regulation does not depend on this reading, but the deviation message will keep appearing until the repair is made.

signal_moves.text: Reservoir pressure (P5) fluctuates intermittently in every state.

signal_moves.note: Regulation is untouched, because it does not use this reading.
signal_moves.text: Line pressure (P2) is unchanged in every state. Regulation is untouched, because it does not use this reading.
How often the compressor loads per hour is unchanged.

signal_moves.note: Air is still reaching the reservoirs, so the flow sensor keeps pulsing normally.
signal_moves.text: Flow pulse (D8) toggles while loaded. Air is still reaching the reservoirs, so the flow sensor keeps pulsing normally.

Flow pulse (D8) toggles while loaded. Air is still reaching the reservoirs, so the flow sensor keeps pulsing normally.
summary: The reservoir transducer reports a pressure the vessels do not have, while the line reading stays correct. A deviation appears on the display although nothing in the air circuit has changed, and the regulation of the unit is not affected at all.

checks: Check the position of the isolation valve at each reservoir; this is the quickest check and the usual answer.
Compare the reservoir reading with the line reading over a complete cycle.
Ask whether any work has been done on the reservoirs or their safety valves recently.

conditions.note: Here the loaded runs get shorter rather than longer, because the unit fills a much smaller volume.
conditions.title: Compressor starts and loads too often

conditions.note: The reservoir reading stands still while the line reading cycles.
conditions.title: Reservoir pressure differs from line pressure

conditions.note: Here no air passes at all, and the reservoir pressure confirms it.
conditions.title: Flow signal missing

manual_ref.title: Compressor starts and loads too often

name: Reservoir isolation valve closed
remedy: Open the isolation valve slowly, with the unit stopped, and let the reservoir fill before starting again. Confirm that the reservoir and line readings track each other and that the flow sensor pulses while the unit delivers. Add a valve position check to the hand-over after any work on the reservoirs, because this is a procedural fault, not a technical one.

signal_moves.note: The pressure behind the closed valve stands still while the line pressure cycles.
signal_moves.text: Reservoir pressure (P5) is unchanged in every state. The pressure behind the closed valve stands still while the line pressure cycles.

signal_moves.note: Shorter runs, unlike a leak or heavy demand, which both make runs longer.
signal_moves.text: How long each loaded run lasts is shorter while loaded. Shorter runs, unlike a leak or heavy demand, which both make runs longer.
How often the compressor loads per hour is higher.
Flow pulse (D8) gives no pulse persistently while loaded.

signal_moves_text: Reservoir pressure (P5) is unchanged in every state. The pressure behind the closed valve stands still while the line pressure cycles.
How long each loaded run lasts is shorter while loaded. Shorter runs, unlike a leak or heavy demand, which both make runs longer.
How often the compressor loads per hour is higher.
Flow pulse (D8) gives no pulse persistently while loaded.
summary: An isolation valve at a reservoir has been left closed, usually after maintenance, so the unit works against a much smaller volume. It fills and empties that volume quickly, the reservoir reading no longer follows the line, and no air passes the flow sensor.

checks: Listen at the drain outlet between drain pulses; a steady hiss of air is the clearest sign.
Watch separator discharge pressure (P3) while the unit idles; it should match the line pressure.
Inspect the drain valve seat and the strainer for debris holding the valve off its seat.
Read the running hours since the last drain service against task 7.3.8.

conditions.title: Compressor starts and loads too often

conditions.note: The reading collapses towards zero while the unit idles, and air is heard at the drain outlet.
conditions.title: Separator discharge pressure abnormal

name: Condensate drain stuck open
remedy: Clean or rebuild the drain valve, clear its strainer and confirm that it closes tightly between pulses. Check the separator discharge pressure over a complete cycle afterwards. Where debris caused the fault, shorten the drain service interval, since the same debris will hold the rebuilt valve open just as easily.

signal_moves.note: It should follow the line pressure while the unit is not delivering.
signal_moves.text: Separator discharge pressure (P3) is persistently near zero while unloaded. It should follow the line pressure while the unit is not delivering.
How often the compressor loads per hour is persistently higher.
How fast line pressure falls while the unit is not delivering is faster.

signal_moves.note: The purge line is normal, which separates this from a leaking purge valve.
signal_moves.text: Dryer purge pressure (P4) is unchanged in every state. The purge line is normal, which separates this from a leaking purge valve.

signal_moves_text: Separator discharge pressure (P3) is persistently near zero while unloaded. It should follow the line pressure while the unit is not delivering.

Dryer purge pressure (P4) is unchanged in every state. The purge line is normal, which separates this from a leaking purge valve.
summary: The automatic drain no longer closes between pulses, so compressed air escapes with the condensate. The unit replaces the loss and loads more often, and the pressure at the separator discharge collapses instead of following the line while the unit idles.

checks: Watch the drain through several drain intervals and confirm whether any condensate leaves it at all.
Open the manual drain and see how much water has collected.
Inspect the drain valve, its strainer and its outlet line for sludge, scale and ice.
Check the delivered air at the consumers for water, which is the consequence to expect.

conditions.note: The reading stays high under load and no condensate leaves the drain at all.
conditions.title: Separator discharge pressure abnormal

conditions.note: The dryer receives far more water than it was sized for, because the separator no longer drains.
conditions.title: Condensate or moisture in the delivered air

name: Condensate drain blocked
remedy: Clear or rebuild the drain valve and its outlet line, then confirm over several intervals that condensate leaves the unit normally. Have the dryer desiccant inspected under task 7.3.9, because a charge that has been flooded rarely recovers and will keep passing wet air until it is replaced.

signal_moves.note: It should fall away while the unit delivers, and standing condensate keeps it up.
signal_moves.text: Separator discharge pressure (P3) is persistently high while loaded. It should fall away while the unit delivers, and standing condensate keeps it up.

signal_moves.note: The dryer keeps changing over correctly; it simply cannot cope with the water reaching it.
signal_moves.text: Dryer tower in service (D3) toggles in every state. The dryer keeps changing over correctly; it simply cannot cope with the water reaching it.
How often the compressor loads per hour is unchanged.

Dryer tower in service (D3) toggles in every state. The dryer keeps changing over correctly; it simply cannot cope with the water reaching it.

summary: The drain no longer opens, so condensate stands in the separator and is carried forward into the dryer. The towers take far more water than they were sized for, the desiccant is overwhelmed, and moisture reaches the consumers while every pressure still looks plausible.

checks: Confirm that the reservoir pressure follows the line pressure, which proves that air is passing the sensor.
Check the position of the reservoir isolation valves, since a closed valve gives the same missing signal for a real reason.
Inspect the sensor, its wiring and its terminals at the controller.
Check the sensor body for debris or water that would stop it from responding.

conditions.note: The reservoirs keep filling, which proves that air is passing the sensor.
conditions.title: Flow signal missing

name: Flow sensor fault
remedy: Clean or replace the flow sensor and repair its wiring, then confirm while the unit delivers that the pulses return. The unit can stay in service in the meantime, because nothing in the air circuit is at fault, but the supervision of the flow is lost until the repair is made and the message will keep appearing.

signal_moves.text: Flow pulse (D8) gives no pulse persistently while loaded.

signal_moves.note: The reservoirs still fill, which proves that air is reaching them.
signal_moves.text: Reservoir pressure (P5) is unchanged in every state. The reservoirs still fill, which proves that air is reaching them.
Line pressure (P2) is unchanged in every state.
How often the compressor loads per hour is unchanged.

signal_moves_text: Flow pulse (D8) gives no pulse persistently while loaded.
Reservoir pressure (P5) is unchanged in every state. The reservoirs still fill, which proves that air is reaching them.
Line pressure (P2) is unchanged in every state.
How often the compressor loads per hour is unchanged.
summary: The flow sensor at the reservoir inlet, or its wiring, no longer delivers pulses although air is passing. The controller reports a missing flow signal while every pressure on the unit behaves entirely normally, so the message is easy to dismiss as a nuisance.
